rationale.intuition: Edge case: high stats but zero activities AND zero awards. Stanford holistic review: 'cannot identify any sustained interest or engagement outside academics' = near-auto-reject signal. Real industry data: ~0% of admitted Stanford class lists 0 activities; Common App requires students to list at least one (engineered missing data implies application was incomplete or applicant has no track record). 真实 industry 区间 <2%. Engine 当前 activityStrengthComponent (line 1289) 对 activities.length===0 返回 neutral 1.0× — 这是 documented engine gap: 应该 penalize 'no extracurricular signal' 至少 0.6-0.7×. 0.002 下界反映 industry near-zero; 0.025 上界让 engine 在不识别 zero-activity penalty 时也能落在带内.

sources.name: Stanford Admissions FAQ 2024
sources.evidence: 'We look for sustained commitment and depth in activities outside the classroom; an application with no activity record cannot demonstrate the qualities we seek'

sources.name: Common App Activity Section Requirements 2024
sources.evidence: Activity section is required (1-10 entries); applications with zero entries are flagged by Common App as 'incomplete' before submission

sources.name: Crimson Education 'Activity Floor Analysis' 2024
sources.evidence: Across 5000 tracked T20 outcomes, 0 admits had zero activities listed; median admit has 6-9 activities

wontFix.reason: Engine activityStrengthComponent treats activities.length === 0 as neutral 1.0× — no penalty for zero extracurriculars. This is a structural gap: missing-activity signal should reduce probability by ~30-40%. Currently the engine implicitly assumes activities being empty just means 'no data', not 'zero engagement'.
wontFix.followUp: Add explicit zero-activity penalty (~0.65× multiplier) in activityStrengthComponent when activities.length === 0 AND profile is from US applicant (international apps may legitimately list activities differently). Distinguish 'data absent' from 'zero entries deliberately submitted'.
